solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: With backing track editor put on over new single's intro

indicators.note: the editor is put on at the end of what comes before
the trail word is laid over the next letters, enclosing them

parts.note: a spoor is the track or trail left by an animal

indicators.note: the intro of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A record producer adds a fresh single's intro to a backing track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With backing' looks like music talk but is the definition: being sponsored means having financial backing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sponsored has a backer paying for it, so it comes with backing.

clue.text: Cause of crack in originally solid lock

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word solid

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Describing how a crack forms inside a solid lock mechanism.
explanation.definitionFit: Mechanical strain is what causes a material to crack, so it is a cause of crack.

clue.text: They've seen it all lost and mired in chaos

indicators.note: being in chaos means these letters are thrown into disorder and rearranged

explanation.surface: People who have seen everything, now lost and stuck in a mess.
explanation.definitionFit: Veterans who have been around a long time have experienced everything, idiomatically seen it all.

clue.text: A break somewhere on the Adriatic?

definitions.meaning: A port city on the Croatian Adriatic coast

explanation.surface: Asking whether a holiday break might be taken on the Adriatic coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A rift or crack is a break, and Split is a real Croatian coastal city.

clue.text: Part for woodwind includes short composition that's struck a chord

indicators.note: the woodwind part includes, that is surrounds, the next piece

parts.note: a reed is the vibrating part of many woodwind instruments

indicators.note: short means the final letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: a sonata is a musical composition

explanation.surface: A woodwind part contains a brief piece that moved its listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part for woodwind' looks like a section of a score, but it is the reed itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that resonated found an echo in people, the idiom for having struck a chord.

clue.text: A short chap tailing Dr No?

indicators.note: tailing means following on behind, so these letters come after

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: short means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a man is a chap

explanation.surface: Asking whether a stunted fellow is following the Bond villain Dr No.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dr No' looks like the film, but Dr belongs to the wordplay; No (also Noh) is the classical Japanese theatre form, an example of the answer, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Noh, also spelt No, is a classical form of Japanese theatre, so it is an example.

clue.text: A lot of hot air from second eleven

parts.note: a cricket or football eleven is a team

explanation.surface: The second eleven's members talk a great deal of hot air.
explanation.definitionFit: Water vapour is literally a lot of hot air rising off boiling water.

clue.text: Find out about dodgy routine I avoided taxing

indicators.note: about means this word goes round the next piece

parts.note: to sus, in British slang, is to find out or work out

indicators.note: dodgy suggests something unreliable, so these letters are rearranged
avoided means this letter is left out of the word

explanation.surface: Discovering that a dubious routine was dodged is a demanding business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dodgy' rearranges what is left once 'I avoided' removes the I, giving TRENUO; 'sus out' is British slang for working something out.
explanation.definitionFit: A strenuous task makes heavy demands, the same sense as a taxing one.

clue.text: Little people having put £ in days before

indicators.note: in means the pound sign goes inside the days word

parts.note: eves are the days before festivals
L, from Latin libra, is the abbreviation for pound sterling

explanation.surface: Small folk who have stashed money in the days before an event.
explanation.definitionFit: Small magical beings of folklore are often called the little people.

clue.text: Notes dog's breakfast taking a long time

indicators.note: taking means the first piece is followed by the next

parts.note: a dog's breakfast is British slang for a mess
ages means a long time

explanation.surface: Jotted notes about a muddle that took forever.
explanation.definitionFit: Short written communications such as notes are messages.

clue.text: Day after day caught up in hassles and problems

indicators.note: caught up in means these letters sit inside the next word

parts.note: to rile someone is to hassle or annoy them

indicators.note: after means one day letter follows the other

explanation.surface: Day after day, someone is caught up in hassles and problems.
explanation.definitionFit: Riddles are puzzling questions, and so problems to be solved.

clue.text: Comes for old documents church put aside for rector

indicators.note: put aside for means the church letters are removed and the rector letter takes their place

parts.note: archives are collections of old documents

explanation.surface: Old church papers are set aside for the rector when he turns up.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrive is to come to a place, so arrives means comes.

clue.text: Struck somebody initially by glove

indicators.note: by means the letter stands beside the next piece
initially points to the opening letter of the word somebody

parts.note: a mitten is a kind of glove

explanation.surface: Someone was hit by a glove, as in a challenge to a duel.
explanation.definitionFit: Smitten is the old past participle of smite, so it means struck, as well as besotted.

clue.text: Diagnosis when a man is confused about experience lately?

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go round the next letter
confused means these letters are jumbled
lately points to the final letter of the word experience

explanation.surface: A doctor's verdict when a man is muddled about what happened recently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' scrambles MAN IS into MNSIA; the question mark flags that forgetting recent experience is the symptom being diagnosed.
explanation.definitionFit: Loss of memory is a medical condition a doctor might give as a diagnosis.

clue.text: Not quite the smallest meadows

indicators.note: not quite means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: least means the smallest

explanation.surface: Fields that are almost the tiniest of all.
explanation.definitionFit: Lea is a poetic word for a meadow or grassland.

clue.text: Reportedly remained stood on head for stability

indicators.note: in a down entry, stood on means the first piece sits above the next
reportedly means a word that sounds like this one is used instead

parts.note: stayed means remained
a ness is a headland, a head jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: Someone who stayed upright on their head showed great balance.
explanation.walkthrough: STAID is pronounced the same as STAYED.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sober and settled in character gives steadiness, a form of stability.

clue.text: I pitch into worn-out crawler

indicators.note: into means these letters go inside the next word

parts.note: trite means worn-out or hackneyed
to lob is to pitch or throw upward

explanation.surface: Someone throws themselves at a tired old creeping creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A fossil marine arthropod that crawled along the sea floor is a crawler.

clue.text: Rambling eglantine, not the cultivated sort

indicators.note: rambling suggests wandering about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wild sweet-briar rose rambling over the hedge, unlike a garden variety.
explanation.walkthrough: Eglantine is the sweet-briar, a wild rose, and rambling roses suit the gardening surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking grace and refinement means not being the cultivated, polished sort of person.

clue.text: He's drunk a beer mixed with rum in it?

indicators.note: mixed with rum, rum meaning odd, signals that the letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A drinker has had a beer laced with rum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like the spirit but is the signal to rearrange A BEER and IN IT together.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, an inebriate is a habitual drunkard, so he is drunk.

clue.text: A target raised — brothers entered Olympic table to hold this?

indicators.note: entered means the brothers go inside the reversed target
in a down entry, raised means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: an aim is a target

explanation.surface: A goal is lifted as siblings join the Olympic banquet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns the target word upwards to MIA, as this is a down entry. The gods of Mount Olympus ate this food.
explanation.definitionFit: The food of the gods of Mount Olympus would be what their table held.

clue.text: Fumble finishing off beery drink added to lime cocktail

indicators.note: added to here means the drink goes into the middle of the next letters
a cocktail is a mixture, so these letters are rearranged
finishing off means the last letter of the word is removed

parts.note: shandy is beer mixed with lemonade

explanation.surface: Botching the mixing of a shandy with a lime cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cocktail' rearranges the fruit to MILE, and 'finishing off' drops the drink's last letter. Shandy is a British drink of beer and lemonade.
explanation.definitionFit: To fumble something is to handle it clumsily, the meaning here.

clue.text: Dashed off second page to editor

explanation.surface: Someone quickly wrote another page to send to the editor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dashed off' suggests quick writing but means hurried away.
explanation.definitionFit: Sped is the past tense of speed, so it means hurried or dashed off.

clue.text: Excited tenor tours Italy to get bearings

indicators.note: tours means the scrambled letters go around the next letter
excited means stirred up, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: An eager singer travels around Italy to find his way.
explanation.definitionFit: To orient oneself is to work out position and direction, getting one's bearings.

clue.text: Without restrictions live at the limits — what's left?

indicators.note: at the limits means the live word sits on both sides of the letter

parts.note: to reside is to live somewhere
U is the British film certificate for universal viewing, with no restrictions

explanation.surface: Living freely on the edge, someone asks what remains.
explanation.walkthrough: A U-rated film is open to all ages, so U stands for 'without restrictions'.
explanation.definitionFit: A residue is the remainder after something is removed, whatever is left over.

clue.text: Removing clothes dive off, do

indicators.note: off means these letters are taken away from the word

parts.note: divesting is stripping off, as in removing clothes

explanation.surface: Undressing for a dive is suggested, but skip the dive itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A sting is a confidence trick, and to do someone is slang for swindling them.

clue.text: Make certain to kill king to succeed

indicators.note: to kill the king means his letter is removed from the word

parts.note: to ensure is to make certain
R, from Latin rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A plotter guarantees the king's murder so he can take the throne.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to follow on afterwards, one sense of succeed.

clue.text: European politician's mistake gutted leader

parts.note: MP, Member of Parliament, is a politician

indicators.note: gutted means the middle letter of the word is taken out

parts.note: an error is a mistake

explanation.surface: A European politician's blunder has devastated their leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' looks like dismay, but it removes the middle R of ERROR.
explanation.definitionFit: The supreme ruler of an empire is its leader.

clue.text: Trouble with duck and sauce involving Basil

indicators.note: with means the next letter is joined on

parts.note: a pest is a troublesome nuisance
a duck is a zero score in cricket, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Someone named Basil causes trouble with a duck dish.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital B makes Basil look like a man's name; it is the herb.
explanation.definitionFit: The Genoese sauce is made from basil leaves, pine nuts, garlic and cheese.

clue.text: Predators on the web? I'd press for a change

indicators.note: for a change means the letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Online hunters, and someone urging a different approach.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunting arachnids sit on their webs awaiting prey, so they are predators there.

clue.text: Banger with a couple of turnovers to allay hunger perhaps

indicators.note: two turnovers means two letter pairs of the word are each flipped round

parts.note: a banger is British slang for a sausage

explanation.surface: A sausage and a couple of pastry turnovers to satisfy hunger.
explanation.walkthrough: Turn over the pairs SA and US in SAUSAGE to get AS and SU. A banger is the British everyday word for a sausage; a turnover is also a pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: To assuage is to soothe or satisfy an appetite, so it fits allaying hunger.

clue.text: Like shielding for instance an individual

definitions.text: Like shielding for instance an individual

indicators.note: shielding means the like word wraps round the following letters

parts.note: as means like
EG is short for exempli gratia, for instance
I, the first person, is one individual

explanation.surface: Something resembling protection for, say, a single person.
explanation.definitionFit: Protection or sponsorship, from the shield of Zeus, is what shields an individual.

clue.text: Confused text about wanderer he's turned out

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go round the next word
confused means these letters are jumbled

parts.note: a rover is a wanderer

explanation.surface: A garbled message about a traveller who has been sent away.
explanation.definitionFit: An outgoing person's attention is turned outward, which the Latin roots of the word literally say.
